This one installs over 2.1.1 the normal way. Same signing key, nothing to uninstall.

## The television client ran on a television

2.1.1 shipped the TV build without it ever having run on real hardware. It has now been
installed on an Android TV box and driven with the remote: the D-pad moves focus through
the rows and playback works. Playback is the part that mattered. The whole reason the TV
flavour exists is libmpv and the codecs it covers, and whether libmpv loads on a 32-bit
TV stick was the one question no emulator could answer.

## Settings subpages open at the top

Opening "about" showed the page already scrolled down, with the name and the version out
of sight above the fold. The settings list and an opened subpage were sharing a single
scroll position, so a subpage started wherever the list had been left. They keep separate
positions now.

## Arrows and dots come from the theme

Picking up where 2.1.1 left off with the tick, the star and the heart. Expand arrows, the
month arrows in the calendar, the bullets in the dashboard and the shortcuts, the folder
marker in the \*arr browser, the seek indicator in the player and the selection dots in
the television menu were all plain characters sitting inside labels. The font decided how
they looked, they could not be coloured with the rest of the row, and a screen reader read
them out loud. They are icons now.

The D-pad help in the television player still writes its arrows as characters. That one is
deliberate: it is describing keys on a remote, not drawing an icon.

## The player screen taken apart

The same work as the four screens in 2.1.1, now for the player. Its five overlays, the
swipe indicator, the seek indicator, the skip button, the next-episode card and the resume
prompt, moved into a file of their own. The `PlayerScreen` composable went from 689 lines
to 565, and the television player from 414 to 397.

Those numbers count the function, not the file. `PlayerScreen.kt` itself only went from
1099 lines to 1063, because the code moved next door rather than disappearing.

## Small print

- The \*arr import dialog marked files it could not match with a bare dash in the
  table cell. It says "unmatched" now.
- The German strings still left in the television client were translated, and its track
  picker became a function of its own.
- The launch smoke test runs again. It had been failing ever since the phone and TV
  flavours were introduced, because it installed the APK from a path that stopped
  existing at that point. The emulator was never the problem; it boots in 36 seconds.

## Installing

- Phone: `sanctumd-v2.1.2.apk`
- Android TV: `sanctumd-tv-v2.1.2.apk`

Both update in place over 2.1.1. The television build installs beside the phone app, not
over it.
